title: Dispatch: ysr3 Animate Objects / Giant Insect 0-HP reversion (Sonnet 5.5, attempt 1)
description:
Implement eshyra-ysr3 (read it: `bd show eshyra-ysr3`). Parent integration bead: eshyra-j3yp. All design decisions below are made; do not re-decide them. If something here contradicts the code or the SRD record text, stop and record the contradiction in your notes rather than improvising.

HARD RULE (bd memory srd-fidelity-hard-blocker): nothing may contradict the SRD. Source text is in packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json (records `spell:animate-objects`, `spell:giant-insect`; read `data.description` and `data.effects[0].profile/transitions`). Do NOT edit records.json or any importer file.

## Source facts
- Animate Objects (profile `animated-object`): "Each target animates and becomes a creature under your control until the spell ends or until reduced to 0 hit points." / "When the animated object drops to 0 hit points, it reverts to its original object form, and any remaining damage carries over to its original object form." Transitions: spell-end-reversion and zero-hp-reversion (effect->ended, form->original; the 0-HP one has operation carry-remaining-damage-to-original-form). The original form is an OBJECT, not a creature.
- Giant Insect (profile `target-transformation`, identity existing-targets, "targets transform in place"): "A creature remains in its giant size for the duration, until it drops to 0 hit points, or until you use an action to dismiss the effect on it." Transitions spell-end-reversion, zero-hp-reversion, action-dismissal-reversion (effect->ended, form->original, scope each-target). The original form is the same CREATURE at natural size. No damage carry-over is stated (contrast Animate Objects), so none is applied.

## Decisions (captain + user, 2026-10-04)
1. Split the durable 0-HP rule value 'revert' into two values:
   - `'revert-object'` (Animate Objects): at 0 HP the creature leaves play exactly like 'vanish' (status absent, never dead/dying/stable/unconscious), its actor link closes (status removed, reason zero-hit-points) and the effect ends (source-removed) when no owned creature remains (reuse closeActorLinkAtZeroHp 'close' mode). The result reports the reversion plus `carriedOverDamage` = damage beyond the hit points it had (`max(0, damage - hpBefore)`; 0 for suffocation drops and exhaustion clamping). The engine does not track object hit points: report the amount, do not invent object state.
   - `'revert-form'` (Giant Insect): at 0 HP by ANY route (damage, suffocation drop, exhaustion clamp to 0; exhaustion 6 is still death) the creature reverts to its recorded natural form and STAYS IN PLAY: status alive, hpCurrent/hpMax/rulesRef restored from the snapshot (decision 2), hpCurrent clamped to the effective max (exhaustion still applies), conditions kept (the same creature; effect-owned condition projections are cleaned by normal link cleanup), zero_hp_rule cleared to null, its actor link closes (status removed, reason zero-hit-points) and the effect ends (source-removed) when no owned creature remains. Never dead/dying/stable/unconscious/absent.
   `vanishesAtZeroHp` currently covers vanish|vanish-bonded; introduce a clearly named predicate for "leaves play at 0 HP" (vanish, vanish-bonded, revert-object) and use it wherever the guards mean "cannot be present at 0 HP / cannot be admitted at 0 HP / absent at 0 HP"; audit every `vanishesAtZeroHp` and `=== 'revert'` site in packages/core/src (combatantLifecycle.ts, encounterCombatants.ts, activeEffects.ts) and route each to the right predicate. The knockout / player-character-death-rules refusals keep applying to all four rule values.
2. Natural-form snapshot (user chose "snapshot at cast"): `start_effect` actors entries gain `naturalForm: { hpCurrent: int > 0, hpMax: int >= hpCurrent, rulesRef: non-empty string }`. REQUIRED when the derived rule is 'revert-form', REFUSED otherwise (including for ruling-sourced actors; `atZeroHitPoints` stays 'vanish' | 'vanish-bonded' only). rulesRef is required so the reverted row never keeps the giant stat-block ref; it need not resolve in the rules stack (lookupCreatureRecord already tolerates unresolved refs; e.g. 'creature:spider' resolves, a centipede has no SRD record). Store it durably on the actor link (new nullable column, decision 4). Reversion restores exactly these values: the hit points it had when transformed.
3. Cleanup policies: add `'revert'` to EffectCleanupPolicy. Derive from the record (extend deriveSummonCleanup / deriveZeroHpRule in packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts, near line 2600):
   - profile `animated-object`: spell-end-reversion -> cleanupOnEnd 'remove'; concentration spell -> cleanupOnBreak 'remove' (the object stops being a creature: it leaves play). A contradicting explicit value (e.g. 'release') is refused with the record's transition id in the message, like the existing derived-policy refusals.
   - profile `target-transformation`: cleanupOnEnd 'revert' and cleanupOnBreak 'revert'; contradictions refused.
   - A form->original zero-hit-points transition on any OTHER profile: throw (unknown reversion target) rather than guess.
   - 'revert' is only legal on an actor link carrying a natural form; refuse it anywhere else (condition/zone/form links, ruling sources, explicit declarations without a snapshot).
   Cleanup action for 'revert': restore the natural form through a new engine seam (mirror removeCombatantFromPlay / removeCampaignActorFromPlay in packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts ~2658-2760: combatant in an active instance, else the campaign actor, delegating to its active combatant projection), then close the link with status 'removed' and report action 'reverted' (add 'reverted' to EffectCleanupAction['action']; do not add a link status). Apply it in cleanupOwnedState (~2286) and removeEffectTarget (~4390, per-target action dismissal) — both currently treat everything that is not 'release' as remove. Unreachable holder -> 'missing' as for remove.
4. Migration `packages/core/data/migrations/0040_*.sql` (follow 0024 and 0039 for the table-rebuild pattern and PRAGMA handling; check how migrationRunner registers/validates migrations):
   - active_effect_link: cleanup_on_end / cleanup_on_break CHECKs add 'revert'; add `natural_form_json TEXT` (NULL unless link_kind = 'actor'; consider a CHECK that 'revert' policies imply link_kind 'actor' AND natural_form_json IS NOT NULL). Keep the zone/form remove-only CHECK.
   - encounter_combatant.zero_hp_rule CHECK becomes ('vanish','vanish-bonded','revert-object','revert-form'). Rewrite existing 'revert' rows: 'revert-object' when any actor link (any status) holding that combatant belongs to an effect whose source_ref = 'spell:animate-objects', otherwise 'revert-form'. Apply the same rewrite to the mirrored campaign-actor lifecycle JSON (`combatLifecycle.zeroHpRule`; find the column via encounterCombatants.ts ~1176-1250 readCombatLifecycle/upsertCampaignActor) and to readCombatLifecycle's accepted values. Nothing has been released since v0.2.0 (2026-06-28), so legacy 'revert-form' rows without a snapshot only exist in dev DBs: durable-state validation reports them, and a 0-HP reversion of such a creature refuses with a message naming the missing natural form (ending/removing its owning effect target still works under its stored legacy policy).
5. validateActiveEffectDurableState (activeEffects.ts ~1490): report a 'revert' policy link without a natural form, a natural form on a non-actor link, and an active 'revert-form' creature with no active snapshot-carrying link.
6. Results and model-facing text. Generalize the update_combatant outcome (encounterCombatants.ts `VanishedOutcome` ~496-510, toolUpdateCombatant.ts ~200-220, exhaustionMutation.ts ~91, the suffocation path ~3308 and toolSetSuffocation.ts text): 'revert-object' reports that the animated object reverted to an object and left play, with carriedOverDamage and the link/effect outcome; 'revert-form' reports a `reverted` outcome with the restored natural form (hpCurrent, hpMax, rulesRef) and the link/effect outcome. Never say "vanished" for a reversion. Update the descriptions in toolUpdateCombatant.ts, toolStartEffect.ts (naturalForm property + cleanup 'revert' + derived policies), toolSetSuffocation.ts, toolStartEncounter.ts if it mentions the rule, toolRemoveEffectTarget/toolEndEffect if they describe cleanup actions. Every model-facing sentence must be re-derived against the source text above and the actual tool contract.
7. docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md: replace the "`revert` ... only feeds the guards; its 0-HP behaviour is pending (eshyra-ysr3)" text in §9 and the §8 remove/absent notes with the executed contract for both values, the 'revert' cleanup policy, the snapshot, and the migration's legacy rule.

## Evidence (packages/core/test/zeroHpVanishAndRemovePolicy.test.ts is the home; add a sibling file only if it grows unwieldy)
Registry-level evidence per source sentence, asserting identities and exact values (no count-pinned assertions):
- Animate Objects: damage past 0 -> status absent (not dead), link removed reason zero-hit-points, carriedOverDamage exact (e.g. hp 7, hpDelta -10 -> 3); last object -> effect ended source-removed; with two objects the effect continues; spell end (end_effect expired/dismissed) and concentration break -> absent via derived 'remove'; explicit cleanupOnEnd 'release' refused; suffocation drop -> absent with carriedOverDamage 0.
- Giant Insect: damage to 0 -> alive with exactly the snapshot hp/hpMax/rulesRef, zeroHpRule null, link removed (zero-hit-points), never dead; exhaustion clamp to 0 and suffocation drop -> same reversion; spell end, concentration break, and remove_effect_target (per-target dismissal) -> reverted in play with action 'reverted'; missing naturalForm refused; naturalForm on a vanish spell or ruling source refused; explicit cleanup 'remove'/'release' refused; knockout and player-character death rules still refused.
- Migration: a DB at 0039 with a 'revert' Animate Objects row and a 'revert' Giant Insect row migrates to 'revert-object' / 'revert-form' (follow migrationRunner.test.ts / migrationLegacyAdoption.test.ts patterns); legacy revert-form without snapshot is reported by validation.
- Replace the existing test "a reverting creature gets the guards but no automatic 0-HP behaviour" (it encodes the pending state and passes release/release, which is now refused). Update persistence/migration tests that enumerate zero_hp_rule values.

## Procedure
Work only in this worktree. Run `npm ci` first if node_modules is missing. Run `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing (it rewrites files); it must be fully green (documented skips only). Commit on this branch with a message starting `eshyra-ysr3`, ending with the line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.

DEVIATIONS/NOTES: (1) Restored combatant ac is taken from the natural rulesRef record when it resolves, else NULL (snapshot has no AC). (2) A dead or absent holder at reversion cleanup reports 'missing'. (3) Closing combat with a combatant concentration owner breaks concentration so Giant Insect creatures revert at combat close (correct per cleanupOnBreak revert); the out-of-combat reversion test therefore uses a character concentrator. (4) closeActorLinkAtZeroHp audit note text for non-reverting case changed from 'disappeared' to 'left play'. (5) A recast concentration replacement re-applies the zero_hp_rule after the replaced effect's cleanup clears it. (6) Pre-existing audit quirk observed: auditActiveEffectIntegrity reports 'persistent actor link still points at combatant' for any active durable-actor link on a combatant even mid-combat.
